meta.title: Pausa · A film diary with friends, and what to watch tonight
meta.description: A free app to keep a private diary of films, series and anime with your friends. And when nobody knows what to watch tonight, vote and decide in 2 minutes.
meta.siteDescription: The private diary of films, series and anime for your group of friends.

og.tagline: The private diary for your friend group.

hero.title: What are we watching tonight? Decided in two minutes.
hero.lede: The private diary of films, series and anime for your friend group: everyone's ratings in one place, and a movie night that picks for you.
hero.note: All you need is an email, no password. Your friends can vote without an account.

mock.title: Chernobyl
mock.review: Five episodes, five knots in the stomach. Marco stopped breathing at the third.

problem.title: Half an hour of messages to pick a film. And three months later nobody remembers what you watched.
problem.body: It happens in every group. Pausa gives you two things: a place to keep what you watch together, and a fast way to decide what to watch next.

how.title: Three steps and the evening is sorted

steps.title: Create the Circle
steps.body: Name the group and send the invite link. Whoever joins sees only your diary, nothing else. The link expires on its own, and you can revoke it whenever you like.

steps.title: Log what you watch
steps.body: Half-star rating, a couple of lines that read like subtitles, who was there with you. Spoilers stay hidden until someone chooses to read them.

steps.title: Decide on the night
steps.body: Open a movie night with a shortlist and send the link. Everyone votes from their phone, even without an account: in two minutes there's a winner and a Card to share.

features.title: Everything a group needs, nothing it doesn't

items.title: A diary for everyone
items.body: Every film, series and anime, with each person's rating, reactions and comments. With “watched with” you know who was there.

items.title: The movie night
items.body: A lightning bracket or a Table with 3 votes and a veto. No more “you pick”.

items.title: How alike you are
items.body: From the real ratings: who shares your taste, what splits you, what to watch together. Your year at a glance.

items.title: Lists and rankings
items.body: Group watchlists, rankings, personal lists. Add a title in one tap.

items.title: A Card to share
items.body: The movie night's result in story format, with the chosen title. Never who voted for what.

items.title: Made for your phone
items.body: Italian, English and Spanish, light or dark. Installs from your Home Screen, no app store.

try.title: Try a movie night, right now
try.body: Four films, two matches, one final. It's exactly what you'll do with your friends, only here it's just you deciding.
try.pick: Pick the one you'd watch tonight.

guest.title: Your friends don't have to sign up
guest.body: To vote in a movie night they just open the link and type a name. No account, no password, no app. It works inside WhatsApp and Instagram too.

items.title: Only who you invite
items.body: The diary is visible only to the Circle's members. There are no public profiles and no global rankings.

items.title: Invites that close
items.body: Links expire, can have a limited number of spots, and are revoked in one tap.

items.title: The Card says little
items.body: What leaves the Circle is only the Card: the chosen title, never who voted for what.

items.title: Leave whenever you like
items.body: You can leave a Circle at any time.

items.a: Right now Pausa has no paid plans: create a Circle and you're in.

items.q: Do my friends need an account?
items.a: Not to vote in a movie night: a name is enough. Keeping the Circle's diary takes an account, with just an email.

items.q: Do I have to install an app?
items.a: No. Pausa works in the browser and can be added to your Home Screen.
Only the members of the Circles you're in. Nothing is public. The only thing that leaves is the Card, if you choose to share it.

items.q: Does it work with series and anime?
items.a: Yes: films, series and anime in the same diary.
Italian, English and Spanish. Each person sees Pausa in their own language, even in the same Circle.

items.q: Where do the posters and data come from?
items.a: From TMDB. Pausa uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.

final.title: Tonight, stop arguing.
final.body: Create the Circle, invite your friends, decide in two minutes.

footer.tagline: The private diary for friend groups.

install.title: Put Pausa on your phone
install.intro: It installs from the browser, no store needed: it gets its own icon and opens full screen.

import.title: Import your history
import.lede: Bring over what you've already watched. You can run it again any time: what's already here isn't duplicated.
import.visibility: You choose where your import goes: by default it stays in your personal space, private, dated when you watched it, and nobody is notified. Reviews are included only if you leave the box ticked.

letterboxd.title: Films from Letterboxd
steps: On Letterboxd go to Settings → Data → Export your data.
Upload it below (diary.csv, ratings.csv, reviews.csv and watched.csv one by one also work).
For lists: open each list on Letterboxd → ··· → Export list as CSV, or use the ZIP (watchlist and the lists/ folder).
letterboxd.pick: Choose the ZIP or the CSV files

anilist.title: Anime from AniList
anilist.body: Your username is all it takes: we read your public list of completed anime straight from AniList. If your profile is private, make it public only for the time of the import.

mal.title: Anime from MyAnimeList
steps: On MyAnimeList go to Profile → Export (myanimelist.net/panel.php?go=export).
Choose “Export My Anime List”: you get an .xml.gz file.
Upload it here without unzipping it.
mal.userBody: Enter your MyAnimeList username (the list must be public). We read it through Jikan, MyAnimeList's public API.

imdb.title: Films and series from IMDb
steps: From the ⋮ menu at the top right choose "Export": shortly after, the file is in "Your exports".
Download the .csv file and upload it here as it is. A list or watchlist export works too.

trakt.title: Films and series from Trakt
steps: On Trakt go to Settings → Data (trakt.tv/settings/data).
Press "Export Data": you get a ZIP of JSON files.
Upload the whole ZIP here, unopened. Or pick the .json files from the watched and ratings folders.
trakt.pick: Choose the ZIP or the .json files

cinemaniac.title: Films and series from Cinemaniac
steps: In the Cinemaniac app (Android) open the menu and go to Settings → Backup.
Make a backup and save it where you can find it (Drive, Downloads…): it is the file "Cinemaniac.bak".
Upload it here as it is. Films you've seen and series you've started become viewings with your ratings; the ones still to watch go to your watchlist.
cinemaniac.dates: Cinemaniac doesn't save when you watched a title, only when you added it to the app: that is the date used. Some old versions of the app broke it, and those titles come in without a date.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: Pausa is a private diary for groups of friends. This explains what data we handle, why, and how you control it.

p: Account: your email and the name you choose (with Google, also your profile picture). If you join a Serata as a guest, only the name you enter.
Content: films, series and anime you log, ratings, reviews, comments, reactions, lists, your "now watching" status, your votes in Serate.
Technical: IP address and user agent of your sessions, for sign-in security and to limit abuse.

Only the members of the Cerchie you belong to. Pausa has no public profiles or public feeds. The only thing meant to leave the app is the Serata Card, which shows the chosen title and not who voted for what.
To provide the service you asked for (contract) and for security and abuse prevention (legitimate interest). We do not profile you for advertising and we do not sell data.
Only strictly necessary cookies: the sign-in session, the light/dark theme and the language. No analytics or advertising cookies, so no consent banner is needed.

Cloudflare: hosting and database. Resend: sending the sign-in email. Google: only if you choose "Sign in with Google". TMDB and AniList: when you search a title, the search (not your identity) is sent to them; posters load from their servers, which therefore see your IP address. If enabled, Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits in aggregate, with no cookies and without identifying you. Title data comes from TMDB (this product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB) and AniList.
Until you delete your account. Deleting a log or a comment removes it immediately. If you leave a Cerchia, your content stays visible to its members until you delete it or delete your account.

From the Account page you can see your data, download it as JSON, fix your name and delete your account at any time: deletion is immediate and removes your logs, comments, reactions and personal lists. You can also ask to restrict or object to processing, and complain to your data protection authority.
For any request about your data, write to the address at the bottom of this page.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: By using Pausa you agree to these simple rules.

p: Pausa is a private group diary for films, series and anime, with a tool to decide together what to watch. It is provided as is, with no guarantee of continuous availability.
You are responsible for what you post in your Cerchie. You must be at least 14 (or the minimum digital age of consent in your country). A Cerchia's admins can remove members and revoke invites.

You keep ownership of what you write. You only give us permission to store it and show it to the members of your Cerchie so the service works. Do not post anything illegal, abusive or that infringes others' rights.
Posters and title information come from TMDB and AniList and remain subject to their terms. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
Do not abuse the service: no unauthorised access attempts, mass sending of invites or sign-in links, or automated use that harms it. We may suspend accounts that do.
You can delete your account at any time from the Account page. We may update these terms; if they change materially we will tell you in the app.

guides.indexTitle: Guides to picking what to watch together
guides.indexLede: Practical ways to decide as a group, without arguing and without losing the evening.

choose-a-movie-with-friends.title: How to choose a movie with friends without arguing
choose-a-movie-with-friends.description: Five methods that actually work for deciding what to watch as a group, from simplest to fastest, and when to use each one.
choose-a-movie-with-friends.intro: Half an hour of scrolling and then watching nothing is the most common movie-night problem. It is not about taste, it is about method. Here are five ways out, fastest first.

p: The trouble is not different tastes, it is endless choice. With two hundred titles on screen nobody commits. Before voting, everyone proposes one title and you end up with six to eight. Under four there is no real choice, over eight the arguing starts again.

blocks.h: 2. One round of voting, with a veto
p: Everyone gets three points to spread and one veto to use once. The veto removes a title with no explanation, and protects the person who would otherwise sit through two hours of a film they hate. Most points wins.

blocks.h: 3. A knockout bracket for indecisive groups
p: Put titles in head-to-head matches: in each one everyone picks one of the two, the most voted goes through. Three rounds are enough for eight titles. It works because comparing two things is easy while ranking eight is tiring.

blocks.h: 4. Whoever chose last time does not choose today
p: A turn rule removes the usual complaint, "you always pick". With a shared diary of what you have watched, it is obvious whose pick was last.

blocks.h: 5. Drop what too many have already seen
p: A film half the group has seen is not a neutral choice: someone rewatches it reluctantly, or spoils it. Remove it before you start.
If deciding takes more than two minutes, the method is too complicated. The point is not to find the perfect film but to stop searching for it.

choose-a-movie-with-friends.cta: Pausa does all of this in two minutes: a roster of eight titles, a quick bracket or a dot-voting table with a veto, and an invite that opens without an account.
